status: hanger candidate shelved after all three bounded support comparisons failed; isolated snap gate passed; full task incomplete

reference.note: Body size chart is not a measured garment pattern. Snap internals and garment dimensions below are estimates.

parameter_provenance: All numeric mechanical parameters are engineering estimates; 0.1356 kg/m2 is converted from the published 4 oz assuming oz/yd2. Manufacturer does not publish force-displacement curves. No hardware was measured.

robot_test.purpose: isolated passive tabletop cloth grasp test

garment.description: Representative simplified sewn long-sleeve shirt; seven identical compatible snap pairs, only uppermost pair is scored. Dimensions and mechanics are estimates. First test starts already on hanger, all snaps open; earns no full-task credit.
garment.mesh_revision_note: Resolve neckline/shoulder hanger contacts at 2 mm; body nominal pitch remains 10 mm. Same physical garment dimensions and material law.
garment.contact_revision_note: Numerical contact refinement: apply contact constraints four times per material solver iteration (native surface-deformable demo uses this setting), after measured 3.95 mm hanger penetration and 27.06% neck-edge strain. Physical material laws and invalidity thresholds unchanged.
garment.neck_revision_note: Estimated round neckline: 60 mm front depth, 20 mm back depth, 160 mm width. Earlier rectangular 60 mm cut on BOTH front/back was an oversimplified shirt pattern with sharp notches. Current curve is in the garment pattern, independent of hanger/fastener target poses; no physical material law changes.
garment.seam_profile_note: Estimated quarter-ellipse fold from sewn edge to panel body, instead of a sharp linear wedge. motivated by stable smooth fabric-sleeve support and repeated bar crossings at the sharp shoulder seam. No change to fabric law, snap geometry or success limits.
garment.seam_join_note: Sewn edges share continuous FEM vertices rather than a narrow extra strip of triangles. This is a local seam representation, with no external attachment or rigidity; all non-seam fabric remains deformable. Earlier bar crossings repeatedly occurred in the narrow strip.

hanger.description: Estimated hollow polymer hanger body with a metal hook, freely supported on a static rail; no world joint or cloth attachment. Shape, effective mass and friction are provisional estimates.
hanger.geometry_revision_note: Balance hook over hanger plane. Earlier hook centre 20 mm behind body caused a large free-body pitch/translation as gravity aligned its centre of mass below the rail; shirt/patch slipped during that transient. Same 25 mm hook radius, 3.5 mm wire radius and 5 mm hanger-bar radius.
hanger.support_layout_note: Posts at Y +/-1.0 m, outside the 1.56 m full sleeve span. Earlier 1.1 m rail put posts through sleeves and was an invalid starting layout.
hanger.bar_geometry_note: Collision diagnostic: replace cylindrical body bars with capsules of the same 5 mm radius and centreline. Only rounded endcaps differ (5 mm beyond line ends); hook/rail unchanged. Test whether analytic capsule contact resolves measured body-bar cloth penetration. Not a change to snap hardware.
hanger.material_assumption_note: A 60 g effective mass is inconsistent with the earlier wording of a solid 10 mm steel wire body. The intended lightweight body is now explicitly a hollow polymer frame with a metal hook. No collider, mass or friction value is changed by this documentation correction; no exact hanger product or measured calibration is claimed.
